title: Ibrahima Konate says he is ‘close’ to new contract: What this means for Liverpool
content:
Ibrahima Konate says he is “close” to signing a new long-term contract at Liverpool.

The France defender, 26, whose current deal expires this summer, has been in talks with the club over an extension since October 2024.

The impasse led to growing speculation over his future but he now expects to stay put following a breakthrough in negotiations.

“For a long time we have spoken with the club and we are close to an agreement,” he told reporters following Sunday’s 2-1 victory over rivals Everton.

“I think everyone wished for that for as long as possible but we are in a good way. For sure, there is a big chance I’m here next season. This is what I always wanted.

“I have a special relationship not only with the fans, but with every single person who works at the club. It’s such an amazing club, amazing family. This club means so much to me.”

Asked why the process had dragged on so long, Konate added: “This is negotiation. With Virgil (van Dijk) and Mo (Salah) last season, it was exactly the same. I think they signed their contracts in April and this is maybe how the club want it.”

Konate, who has made 178 appearances for the club since arriving for £36million from RB Leipzig in 2021, expects Liverpool to be back challenging for trophies next season following a transitional campaign for Arne Slot’s side and the impending summer exits of Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson.

“The legends are going to leave and after that it’s going to be our turn to take the lead,” he said. “I need the help of everyone as well. I cannot do it alone.

“It’s been a bad season for the standards of Liverpool. If we finish in the top four, we won’t be happy, for sure. We have to give our all next season to make something good.”

Konate struggled for form in the first half of the campaign and went on compassionate leave after losing his father in January. He returned earlier than planned to help the team, and his performances have been much improved in the second half of the season.

“It was a tough year because many things happened and I think if everyone knew exactly what happened to me, they could understand many things, which kind of sacrifices I’ve done for this club,” he added.

“Right now I am focused on the end of the season and making sure we are qualified for the Champions League. After, we’ll take the time to talk about this season because it’s going to be a big part of my story. It’s sad in one part, but it’s very nice for my story when I explain that to my future kids and those people who support this club as well.”

Ibrahima Konate staying at Liverpool feels like a common sense outcome for all parties following a protracted contract saga.

The Athletic reported earlier this month that multiple sources with links to the dressing room expected the centre-back to belatedly pen a new deal.

Liverpool have always wanted to retain his services but not at any price. There had been a sizeable gap between what they were willing to pay him and what he was demanding.

With Real Madrid withdrawing their interest in Konate before Christmas and Bayern Munich’s need easing in February when Dayot Upamecano extended his contract, it was increasingly difficult to see what other elite European club the 26-year-old defender could have joined this summer.

Konate has had a difficult season at Liverpool but he remains first choice alongside Virgil van Dijk and is a popular member of Arne Slot’s squad.

Trying to replace him this summer would have been a lot more expensive than renewing his contract on improved terms. With Jeremy Jacquet arriving from Rennes and fellow young centre-back Giovanni Leoni returning from a serious knee injury, it means Liverpool are well stocked in the centre-back department, even if Joe Gomez moves on.

With other priorities to address in the transfer market this summer, not having to fill a void created by Konate moving on is a welcome boost.
